headlines.title: US Stock Futures Steady Ahead of Key August Jobs Data
headlines.summary: The August payrolls print is the whole tape right now — with the Fed sitting on a live rate-hike decision and bond vigilantes already rattling the long end, a weak number could flip the script fast. Consensus is looking for just 53,000 jobs added, which tells you the labor market has cooled considerably; a miss or a beat moves every asset class simultaneously. This is the kind of number that sets the tone for September trading across SPY, TLT, and the dollar.

headlines.title: Oil rallies for the week as U.S.-Iran fighting resumes; diesel hits record high
headlines.summary: Renewed U.S.-Iran fighting with the Strait of Hormuz still choked is a genuine supply shock — retail diesel at a record $5.85 a gallon is already bleeding into transportation costs, airline bonds, and consumer inflation expectations. This hits energy names (USO, XLE) to the upside while hammering airlines, truckers, and any company with fat fuel bills; it also keeps the Fed's inflation problem alive heading into the September meeting. Geopolitical stories have been my best-performing category, and this one has real teeth.

headlines.title: World's biggest sovereign wealth fund plans to cut U.S. Treasury holdings
headlines.summary: Norway's $2.3 trillion fund stepping back from Treasuries is a structural bid-removal story at exactly the wrong moment — bond vigilantes are already pushing yields higher and the market is fragile ahead of payrolls. A sovereign seller of this size adds fuel to the global bond selloff that El-Erian is warning isn't over, which ripples directly into equity valuations via the discount rate. Watch TLT and the long bond; if yields spike on this, the equity rally stalls fast.
